holder_verification_steps: 1. Before accepting: record in writing which authorship records you checked (skill files; every replay_cases.csv and cases.csv listed in RECEIPT_TEMPLATE item 4) and that you authored none of them. The PI's assertion does not replace your own statement.

2. Receive the six files and PACKAGE_SHA256SUMS out of band from someone who can read the working tree (not from a panel agent). Check sha256 of PACKAGE_SHA256SUMS against package_manifest_sha256 above, then run `sha256sum -c PACKAGE_SHA256SUMS` from the repository root or on your copies with the same relative paths. Every line must read OK; any mismatch voids the corresponding seal and must be reported, not repaired.
3. Recompute each polarity file from its cases.csv in the canonical form above and confirm byte equality. Confirm each cases.csv still has the extracted_from_sha256 above.

4. Optionally recompute each id map from OPAQUE_ID_RULE.md (python3 astronomy/wave3/agent5_integrity/scripts/make_opaque.py in a scratch copy) and confirm byte equality; the rule is deterministic from the brief hash.
5. Complete RECEIPT_TEMPLATE.txt, return it; the coordinator writes its sha256 into receipt_hash and sets status COMPLETE.

6. After receipt: have the coordinator remove from anything the stage under test can read both RULINGS_SEALED.csv files, the polarity columns (cases.csv and the committed astronomy/replay/evaluator/score_*.txt, which list polarity per case), and all id maps; record the commit at which that happened. Until then the seal is procedural.
7. Run scripts/rescore.py yourself (optionally --with-rulings) on the evaluator's verdict file only after its sha256 is in the order-of-operations log.
8. For a seal that carries weight, write new sealed cases no panel agent has seen (references/replay.md, 'The limit that matters').
known_leaks_not_closed_by_this_package: cases.csv of both suites still carries polarity in the working tree and in git history.

The source-suite K/N id prefixes remain in fm-advantage-benchmark/cases/cases.csv and RULINGS_SEALED.csv (issue 09); only the blind files are re-keyed.
Inputs in the blind files are verbatim cases.csv text, so any reader of cases.csv can map them back. The opaque ids only help an evaluator confined to the blind file.
